title: The Human Body: Working Systems
description: Grade 5 Science: the human body and its systems — digestion, breathing (respiratory), the heart and blood (circulatory), and bones, muscles and the brain. Label the organs and explore.

topics.title: Our Body Is a Team
topics.concept:
Our body is made of tiny living building blocks called cells. Groups of cells form organs like the heart, lungs and stomach. Organs that work together to do a big job form an organ system.

  • 🍽️ The digestive system breaks down food.
  • 🫁 The respiratory system helps us breathe.
  • ❤️ The circulatory system moves blood around.
  • 🦴 The skeletal system holds us up.

All the systems work as a team to keep us alive and healthy.

wonder.text: Right now, without you thinking about it, your heart beats, your lungs breathe and your stomach digests. How does it all work together?

qa.a: A cell is the tiniest living building block of the body. You are made of billions of them! Different cells build different parts — muscle cells, blood cells, skin cells and more.
An organ system is a group of organs that work together for one big job. For example, the mouth, stomach and intestines together form the digestive system.

topics.title: The Digestive System
topics.concept:
The digestive system breaks food into tiny bits the body can use. Food takes a journey:

  • 👄 Mouth — teeth chew the food and saliva softens it.
  • ⬇️ Food pipe — carries food down to the stomach.
  • 🫃 Stomach — churns and breaks the food down further.
  • 🌀 Small intestine — takes the goodness (nutrients) into the blood.

The leftover waste leaves the body when we go to the toilet.

Path: mouth → food pipe → stomach → small intestine.
Nutrients pass into the blood; waste leaves the body.

wonder.text: When you eat a roti, where does it go, and how does your body get energy from it?

qa.q: Why must we chew food well?
qa.a: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva. This makes it easier for the stomach to digest, so we get more goodness from our food.

qa.q: Where is the food's goodness taken in?
qa.a: In the small intestine. The digested nutrients pass through its walls into the blood, which carries them to every part of the body.

topics.title: Breathing: The Respiratory System
topics.concept:
The respiratory system takes in the air we need and removes air we do not.

  • 👃 We breathe IN air through the nose.
  • 🫁 Air goes down to two lungs in the chest.
  • 💨 The lungs take in oxygen (which the body needs) and pass it to the blood.
  • ♻️ We breathe OUT a waste gas called carbon dioxide.

recap: We breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.

wonder.text: You breathe about 20,000 times a day without trying. What happens to the air inside you?

qa.q: Why do we breathe faster after running?
qa.a: Running makes muscles work hard, so they need more oxygen. We breathe faster and deeper to take in extra oxygen and remove the extra waste gas.

qa.q: What does the body do with oxygen?
qa.a: The body uses oxygen to get energy from food, in every cell. Without oxygen, our cells could not make energy — which is why breathing never stops!

topics.title: The Heart and Blood
topics.concept:
The circulatory system carries blood all around the body. At its centre is the heart — a strong muscle that pumps blood.

  • ❤️ The heart pumps blood through tubes called blood vessels.
  • 🩸 Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of the body.
  • ♻️ It also carries away waste.
  • 💓 You can feel your heartbeat as your pulse.

recap: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood.
Blood carries oxygen and food, and removes waste.
We feel the heartbeat as our pulse.

wonder.text: Your heart squeezes about once every second, all day and all night, for your whole life. What is it pumping?

qa.a: Blood is the body's delivery service! It carries oxygen and food to every cell, and takes away waste. It travels round and round, pushed by the heart.

qa.q: Where can I feel my pulse?
qa.a: Press two fingers gently on your wrist or the side of your neck. The little throb you feel is your pulse — your heart pumping blood with every beat!

topics.title: Bones, Muscles and the Brain
topics.concept:
Three more amazing systems keep us moving and thinking:

  • 🦴 Skeleton (bones) — gives the body its shape, holds it up and protects organs (the skull guards the brain).
  • 💪 Muscles — pull on bones to make us move, run and lift.
  • 🧠 Brain — the control centre. It thinks, remembers and sends messages to the whole body.

recap: The skeleton supports and protects the body.
Muscles pull on bones to make us move.
The brain is the control centre that thinks and sends messages.

wonder.text: What holds you up, lets you move, and is the boss of your whole body?

qa.q: How do bones and muscles work together?
qa.a: Muscles are joined to bones. When a muscle tightens, it pulls the bone and the body part moves. Bending your arm, the muscle pulls the lower arm up — try it!

qa.q: Why is the skull so hard?
qa.a: The skull is hard bone that protects the soft, precious brain inside, like a strong helmet. It keeps your control centre safe from bumps.

questions.q: The tiniest living building block of the body is a…
questions.explanation: Cells are the tiniest living building blocks; groups of them form organs.
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body.

questions.q: We breathe in oxygen using our…
questions.explanation: The lungs take in oxygen when we breathe.

questions.q: Food is broken down in the…
questions.explanation: The digestive system breaks down the food we eat.
The hard skull bone protects the soft brain inside.

questions.q: We breathe OUT a waste gas called…
questions.explanation: We breathe out carbon dioxide, a waste gas.

questions.q: Why do we breathe faster after running?
options: Muscles need more oxygen, so we take in more
questions.explanation: Hard-working muscles need more oxygen, so we breathe faster to supply it.

questions.q: Where does the food's goodness pass into the blood?
questions.explanation: Nutrients pass into the blood through the walls of the small intestine.

questions.q: How do muscles move our bones?
options: They tighten and pull on the bones
questions.explanation: Muscles tighten and pull on bones to make the body move.

questions.q: Put the digestion journey in order.
options: Mouth → food pipe → stomach → small intestine
questions.explanation: Food travels mouth → food pipe → stomach → small intestine.

questions.q: Which best describes the body's organ systems?
options: They work together as a team to keep us alive
questions.explanation: All the organ systems work together as a team to keep us alive and healthy.
